evidence: A model result of an offline chain on the design years, A28R_301k_design_l15_snow_s934 years 10-19 on PlaSim's T21 grid, with no feedback on the climate: each 3-day mean's convective rain as point storms from a library, the large-scale rain as a steady 2 mm/h (an estimate), and Green and Ampt infiltration at lunar gravity (conductivities times g, suction heads over g) into four designed surfaces whose Earth parameters are texture-class means (Rawls et al. 1983) and a seal from Rawls et al. (1990). The Walnut Gulch library is a two-parameter family fitted to Earth's measured point storms (Osborn 1983) and the CM1 library is CM1's model storms over wet equatorial ground at 6 km and ten minutes; neither is the drylands' own storms. The soil at storm time reads PlaSim's 0.5 m bucket, which the arid, semi-arid and dry sub-humid cells keep 0.4%, 2.7% and 8% full on average. Runoff here is what leaves the point as infiltration excess; it is not routed, and nothing of it is yet lost along slopes and channels or returned by pools. The surfaces are design choices, not measured lunar soils. Phase 2a (phase2a) replaces the two wetting treatments with a redistribution and drying model between storms at random times within each mean (wetting.py) and routes the central runoff on geography's 1.9 km grid into its depression tree (routing.py): run-on infiltration on 100 m slopes, sub-grid crater bowls from the terrain study's equilibrium counts for young and mature land, Lane's channel losses recast for gravity, and storms' runoff-making cores of 5 km2, a value the Walnut Gulch basin check sets. Every routing parameter is a design choice or an Earth value; nothing in the lunar routing is measured. Phase 2b (phase2b) runs every fed depression and the bowls below the grid through the design years: an energy balance of each pool and its floor under the design years' air by tenth (Penman's evaporation by day, the stored heat and night air at night), seepage through designed clay floors or sandy banks at lunar gravity, and fill and spill along the depression tree; the slopes' wear from WEPP's Earth erodibilities with the lunar drops and shear; the salts from designed solute inputs. Its pools, leverage and wet-patch layer are model results on designed floors and stand-in storms.
reading_rule: Ratios are runoff over all rain (convective and large-scale) of the same cells and means, area-weighted over classes. walnut_gulch and cm1_6km bracket the storms' intensities from above and below; independent and continuing bracket the wetting between a mean's storms (each on the mean's soil, or one front carried through them). sealed_loam keeps a formed seal; sealed_loam_forming forms it during each storm under the lunar drops' kinetic energy. by_tenth lists the ten tenths of the lunar day from the one centred 162 degrees before noon to the one 162 after, noon falling between the fifth and sixth; null where a tenth brings under a thousandth of the cell's rain. share_of_evaporation is the runoff over the class's evaporation, an upper bound on the change of the slopes' evaporation before pools return any of it. Volumes are km3 a year of 365.25 days; storms are expected point counts. In phase2a, wetting gives each surface's central runoff ratio with its low and high over the soil curves' range; routing.fates give each fate of the runoff (bowls_inside, slope_soil, bowls_slope, channel_bed, bowls_channel, depressions, sea, humid_land, and the parts of the slopes' and beds' losses below the root zone, slope_recharge and bed_recharge) as shares of the runoff and of the rain, per hollow state (young: bowls of 10 m and more; mature: of 100 m and more); leverage gives the share of the rain leaving the soil's evaporating store (all fates but the soil above the root zone) over the evaporation. The cells' runoff_ratio_2a is the central runoff; routed_walnut_gulch gives mm a year over the cell, by tenth, attributed to the cell where each loss or delivery happens. Per-depression inflow by tenth is in the ignored file named by phase2a.hollow_inflow, rebuilt by run.py. In phase2b, pools give per library, surface, seepage case and hollow age the depressions' and bowls' (wall-fed and channel-fed) numbers in each persistence class, their water's fates in km3 a year and their depths; leverage gives the drylands' evaporation change with the pools as a share of the bucket's, by year and by tenth under two timings of the bucket's loss (the tenth the water runs off, or spread as the bucket's evaporation is); wear gives the slopes' soil loss in mm a year; salts the share of hollows whose floors turn saline within each span; the cells' pools_2b_walnut_gulch_clay_floored give each surface's wet share, pools' evaporation and seepage in mm a year over the cell and the slopes' loss. The wet-patch layer is results/wet_patches.json.

walnut_gulch.source: Osborn (1983), WRR 19(4):1036-1042, Table 1 (fitted); Mendez, Goodrich and Osborn (2003), JAWRA 39(3):611-621, Tables 1-4 (held out)
walnut_gulch.evidence: A parametric family fitted to measured point statistics of Earth's thunderstorms at Walnut Gulch; Earth's storms, not the Moon's

cm1_6km.evidence: CM1 model result: the rain beneath each whole tracked core, its largest 6 km column at each ten-minute output; a floor on point intensities

walnut_gulch_check.rule: Set before the chain was run: it passes when the Walnut Gulch storms at Earth's gravity on the two Walnut Gulch-like soils, each storm on soil at the wilting point, give yearly runoff ratios whose span overlaps the measured 3-10% of the small watersheds; the measured geometric mean over the chain's (sandy loam and loam) is carried to the lunar bare-soil ratios as their Earth factor.

wetting.model: Smith, Corradini and Melone (1993) redistribution with drying between storms at uniformly random times within each mean; Brooks and Corey curves (Rawls et al. 1982 via GSSHA/SWMM5 tables; Ks = 2 K_GreenAmpt, Rawls et al. 1983 eq. 6)

lossless_loam_walnut_gulch.note: the rest joins lakes and depressions that spill with the climatology's own water

walnut_gulch_basin.rule: Set before the chain was run: it passes when the geometric mean of the two soils' yields at the basin's outlet lies within a factor of 3 of the measured 2 mm a year, the factor allowing for the basin's soils spanning both textures and for the measured yield's year-to-year spread.

design.transfer: COARE 3.0 (Fairall et al. 2003) at lunar gravity on the wind with the layer's gust

earth_crust.source: Eldridge et al. 2020, Global Change Biology 26, 6003-6014: sediment production -68% across studies, -85% on loams

design.bowl_shape: paraboloid, Pike's fresh form at half its depth

rule.note: the bulk transfer at Earth's gravity with the measured water-surface temperature, air vapour pressure and the period's mean wind gives the period's latent heat within 25% of the Bowen-ratio energy budget's 164 W/m2 (Moreo and Swancar 2013, Table 4)

over the semi-arid cells, the day's evaporation of a 0.3 m pool lies within 0.8-2.0 times Priestley and Taylor's demand at water's albedo (the plan: small pools in dry air up to about twice it), and the night's within 2.5-30 mm, a factor of two around the plan's 5-15 mm

over the semi-arid cells, the day's evaporation of a 0.3 m pool lies within 0.8-2.0 times Priestley and Taylor's demand at water's albedo (the plan: small pools in dry air up to about twice it), and the night's within 2.5-30 mm, a factor of two around the plan's 5-15 mm

storm library.tested_by: Walnut Gulch: the family against Osborn's counts (fitted) and Mendez's annual maxima (held out); no check of the lunar storms exists until the dry box runs

wetting between storms.tested_by: none: Walnut Gulch's storms come days apart, so its runoff cannot separate the two treatments

soil at storm time.tested_by: Walnut Gulch chain at the wilting point and air-dry

surface retention.tested_by: Walnut Gulch chain (it carries the 1 mm store)

conductivity.tested_by: Walnut Gulch chain on two textures; the gravity factor analytically

suction.tested_by: Walnut Gulch chain on two textures; the gravity factor analytically

seal formation.tested_by: the seal's resistance reproduces Rawls et al.'s crust factor; the drops' energy against the rain solver

biocrust conductivity.tested_by: none beyond the measured range of reductions
